Project Architect, Architecture + Emerging Technology
Spacematter | New York City, NY | Full-Time
Experience: 8–14 Years
Salary: $100,000–$140,000 annually
About Spacematter
Spacematter is an AI-powered architecture and technology company rethinking how buildings are designed, documented, and delivered.
We are expanding our New York City architectural team and seeking an experienced Project Architect who brings a strong foundation in traditional architectural practice and a genuine interest in emerging technologies.
Our work combines the rigor of conventional architectural project delivery with the potential of AI, automation, and computational design to improve how architects work.
The Role
We are looking for a technically accomplished Project Architect who can lead architectural documentation, coordinate consultants, and help deliver projects from design development through construction.
This is a hands-on architectural position, not a software development role. You will work directly with an experienced architectural director on real projects while collaborating with our technology team to help shape new architectural workflows.
Key Responsibilities
Qualifications
Why Join Us?
At Spacematter, we believe technology should empower architects, not replace them.
You'll join a growing team where architectural expertise remains central to the design process. You'll work directly with one of our architectural directors, not an AI system, while gaining exposure to the development of next-generation architectural tools.
This is an opportunity for an architect who values the fundamentals of the profession but is excited to participate in its evolution.
Compensation
Annual salary: $100,000–$140,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
How to Apply
Please submit your resume and portfolio to [email protected] including examples of construction documentation and technically developed architectural projects.
Email subject: Project Architect – NYC
We welcome candidates who are passionate about architecture, curious about technology, and interested in building a new model for architectural practice.
